---
title: Converters
description: Building INIF documents from raw text and from eval-framework outputs.
llms-description: INIF ships converters for raw text, Inspect AI eval logs, and every_eval_ever instance records; all share a common tokenizer-resolution rule.
---

INIF is a sink for tokenized generation traces. The converters in
[`inif.converters`](../reference/inif.converters.text.qmd) translate from
the format produced by your generation pipeline into an
[`InifDocument`](../concepts/format.qmd).

| Source | Module | Entry point |
|---|---|---|
| [Raw text / chat messages](text.qmd) | `inif.converters.text` | `from_texts`, `from_text_files` |
| [Inspect AI eval logs](inspect_ai.qmd) | `inif.converters.inspect_ai` | `from_eval_log`, `from_eval_file` |
| [every_eval_ever records](evaleval.qmd) | `inif.converters.evaleval` | `from_instance_records`, `from_eval_json`, `from_hf_dataset` |

All of them follow the same conventions:

- **Tokenization is mandatory.** Every Sample carries a `tokens` list.
  There is no opt-out — see [Tokenizer resolution](tokenizers.qmd) for
  how the tokenizer is chosen.
- **Sequence deduplication runs by default.** Pass `deduplicate=False` to
  skip it.
- **Chat role tagging is on by default** for the eval converters
  (`tag_chat_roles=True`). The text converter has it off by default
  (chat inputs are detected per element and tagged when present, but the
  default text input is plain string).

## Picking the right converter

- You have raw strings or chat messages produced by something other than an
  eval framework — use the [text converter](text.qmd).
- You have Inspect AI `.eval` log files — use the
  [Inspect AI converter](inspect_ai.qmd). Per-token logprobs and
  generated-output annotations are attached automatically when present.
- You have evaleval JSON / JSONL or want to pull straight from the
  [`evaleval/EEE_datastore`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/evaleval/EEE_datastore)
  HF dataset — use the [evaleval converter](evaleval.qmd). Reasoning-trace
  spans, multi-turn / agentic interactions, tool calls, and aggregate
  metric metadata are preserved.

## Common pitfalls

::: {.callout-warning appearance="minimal"}
#### Closed-source model ids

Auto-loading the tokenizer from `eval_log.eval.model` fails for closed
models (`openai/gpt-4`, `anthropic/claude-3-...`) because there is no HF
tokenizer to fetch. Pass `tokenizer="<hf-stand-in>"` explicitly. The
warning that gets emitted on mismatch is informational — token-level data
will reflect the supplied tokenizer, not the original model.
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="minimal"}
#### Tokenizers that are lossy on per-token decode

A few tokenizers (notably old SentencePiece slow tokenizers, and Qwen,
which replaces U+2028 with U+FFFD) cannot reliably reconstruct per-token
strings. The converters silently skip role / generated / reasoning
tagging for those samples rather than raise. The tokens themselves are
still correct.
:::
